description: Workbench-reviewed closure/source/evidence gap contrast seed batch. Targets misleading versus false, disputed versus debunked, clip versus full record, hearsay versus primary evidence, summary versus underlying record, and not-disproven versus supported.

entries.text: The claim is misleading because it omits the qualifying footnote.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The claim is misleading because it omits the qualifying footnote.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence marks misleading framing, omission, or scope distortion without treating it as direct falsity.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Footnote evidence is legitimate as qualifying context only when it directly limits, defines, or conditions the relevant claim.
Misleading language is legitimate when framing, omission, scope distortion, or presentation creates a false impression without requiring direct falsity.
Omission pressure is legitimate when a relevant qualifying record or context is left out of the claim presentation.

evidence_burden: Identify the footnote.
Map it to the claim.
Check whether it narrows, defines, or merely comments on the claim.
Identify the exact claim or presentation being called misleading.
Identify the omitted, narrowed, or distorted context.
Separate misleading framing from direct falsity.
Identify what was omitted.
Check whether the omitted context is relevant to the claim.
Check whether the omission changes support, scope, or interpretation.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate misleading/framing pressure from direct falsity
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: inspect the evidence object and fuller record before support/contradiction movement
questions: What omitted, narrowed, or distorted context makes the claim misleading rather than false?
What exactly was omitted, and does the omission change support, scope, or interpretation?

entries.text: The headline is misleading even though the quoted number is real.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The headline is misleading even though the quoted number is real.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence marks misleading framing, omission, or scope distortion without treating it as direct falsity.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Misleading language is legitimate when framing, omission, scope distortion, or presentation creates a false impression without requiring direct falsity.

evidence_burden: Identify the exact claim or presentation being called misleading.
Identify the omitted, narrowed, or distorted context.
Separate misleading framing from direct falsity.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate misleading/framing pressure from direct falsity
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: What omitted, narrowed, or distorted context makes the claim misleading rather than false?

entries.text: The clip shows only part of the exchange.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The clip shows only part of the exchange.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence uses a partial clip as evidence and requires the fuller record before strong support or contradiction.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Clip evidence is legitimate only as partial evidence until the fuller record and surrounding context are checked.

evidence_burden: Identify the clip source.
Identify what part of the record is missing.
Compare the clip to the full record before support or contradiction movement.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: treat clip as partial evidence and ask for the fuller record
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: inspect the evidence object and fuller record before support/contradiction movement
questions: What does the full record show beyond the clip?

entries.text: The full transcript gives more context than the clip.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The full transcript gives more context than the clip.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence compares fuller record contact against partial clip evidence.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Transcript evidence is legitimate only when authentic, complete enough for the claim, and mapped to the exact statement.
Clip evidence is legitimate only as partial evidence until the fuller record and surrounding context are checked.

evidence_burden: Identify transcript source.
Check completeness.
Map exact quote or absence claim.
Identify the clip source.
Identify what part of the record is missing.
Compare the clip to the full record before support or contradiction movement.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: compare full transcript contact against partial clip evidence
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: inspect the evidence object and fuller record before support/contradiction movement
questions: What does the full record show beyond the clip?

entries.text: The claim is disputed by several reviewers.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The claim is disputed by several reviewers.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence says the claim is contested; this is dispute pressure, not refutation or falsity.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: A challenge is legitimate as pressure against certainty, but it is not the same as refutation or contradiction.
Reviewer status is legitimate as role metadata; it does not establish the reviewed claim without reasoning and evidence.
Disputed language is legitimate as contestation pressure, but it is not the same as refutation, contradiction, or falsity.

evidence_burden: Identify what part of the claim is challenged.
Identify the reason or evidence for the challenge.
Check whether the challenge weakens, contradicts, or merely questions the claim.
Identify the reviewer.
Identify review role and scope.
Inspect reasoning, criteria, and evidence.
Identify who disputes the claim.
Identify the reason or evidence for the dispute.
Check whether the dispute weakens, contradicts, or merely contests the claim.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: preserve dispute status without converting it into debunking or falsity
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat reviewer/source status as metadata, not truth
questions: Who disputes the claim, and does the dispute weaken, contradict, or merely contest it?

entries.text: The policy result is disputed, but it has not been disproven.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The policy result is disputed, but it has not been disproven.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence says the claim is contested and not yet falsified; neither condition establishes support.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: A challenge is legitimate as pressure against certainty, but it is not the same as refutation or contradiction.
Disputed language is legitimate as contestation pressure, but it is not the same as refutation, contradiction, or falsity.
Not-disproven language is legitimate only as absence of refutation; it does not establish that the claim is true.

evidence_burden: Identify what part of the claim is challenged.
Identify the reason or evidence for the challenge.
Check whether the challenge weakens, contradicts, or merely questions the claim.
Identify who disputes the claim.
Identify the reason or evidence for the dispute.
Check whether the dispute weakens, contradicts, or merely contests the claim.
Identify what would disprove the claim.
Check whether contradictory evidence exists.
Separate not disproven from supported.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: preserve dispute and not-falsified status without converting either into support or falsity
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: Who disputes the claim, and does the dispute weaken, contradict, or merely contest it?
What would disprove the claim, and is there positive support or only lack of refutation?

entries.text: The witness heard the claim secondhand.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The witness heard the claim secondhand.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence uses secondhand or hearsay sourcing and requires primary evidence before claim movement.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Hearsay is legitimate only as source-distance pressure; it does not prove or disprove the underlying claim without primary evidence.

evidence_burden: Identify the original source if possible.
Separate repeated claim from direct evidence.
Seek the document, record, or firsthand testimony.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate secondhand claim transmission from primary evidence
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat hearsay/source-distance as low-contact source pressure, not claim truth
questions: What primary evidence or firsthand source exists beyond the hearsay?

entries.text: The source repeated hearsay without seeing the document.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The source repeated hearsay without seeing the document.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence uses secondhand or hearsay sourcing and requires primary evidence before claim movement.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Hearsay is legitimate only as source-distance pressure; it does not prove or disprove the underlying claim without primary evidence.

evidence_burden: Identify the original source if possible.
Separate repeated claim from direct evidence.
Seek the document, record, or firsthand testimony.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate secondhand claim transmission from primary evidence
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat hearsay/source-distance as low-contact source pressure, not claim truth
questions: What primary evidence or firsthand source exists beyond the hearsay?

entries.text: The summary leaves out the qualifying sentence.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The summary leaves out the qualifying sentence.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence says relevant qualifying context was omitted, creating misleading or qualification pressure.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Omission pressure is legitimate when a relevant qualifying record or context is left out of the claim presentation.
A summary is an interpretation or compression layer and must be checked against the underlying record before claim movement.

evidence_burden: Identify what was omitted.
Check whether the omitted context is relevant to the claim.
Check whether the omission changes support, scope, or interpretation.
Identify the underlying record.
Check what the summary includes or omits.
Compare the summary to the exact record text or data.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: identify omitted context and test whether it changes scope, support, or interpretation
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat summary/source/status as interpretation or metadata, not truth
questions: What exactly was omitted, and does the omission change support, scope, or interpretation?
What underlying record does the summary compress, and what does it include or omit?

entries.text: The summary simplifies the record but does not quote it directly.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The summary simplifies the record but does not quote it directly.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence uses a summary as an interpretation layer that must be checked against the underlying record.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: A summary is an interpretation or compression layer and must be checked against the underlying record before claim movement.

evidence_burden: Identify the underlying record.
Check what the summary includes or omits.
Compare the summary to the exact record text or data.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: treat summary as interpretation layer until checked against the underlying record
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat summary/source/status as interpretation or metadata, not truth
questions: What underlying record does the summary compress, and what does it include or omit?
